valid_fixes: Change the second ES resource in LambdaRole's policy from '${MovieSearchDomain.DomainArn}/other_index/*' back to '${MovieSearchDomain.DomainArn}/*' to cover all index paths under the domain
invalid_patches: Removing the domain-level ARN entry instead of fixing the wildcard suffix entry
Adding a separate Allow statement for the movies index instead of fixing the wildcard suffix
optimal_diagnostic_path: ace_get_log_tail(FunctionName=SearchFunction) → logs show HTTP 403 from Elasticsearch when posting to movies/_search
ace_get_environment_variables(FunctionName=SearchFunction) → ELASTICSEARCH_ENDPOINT and ELASTICSEARCH_INDEX are both correct
ace_get_iam_role(RoleName=LambdaRole) → ES resource list shows DomainArn and DomainArn/other_index/* — the wildcard suffix covers other_index not movies
ace_simulate_policy(RoleArn=LambdaRole, Action=es:ESHttpPost, Resource=arn:...:domain/.../movies/_search) → implicitDeny, confirming the policy gap
observable_symptom: The ingest endpoint accepts movie documents and returns 200. Direct inspection of the search index confirms documents are indexed. The search endpoint returns a 403 error for every query. Search function logs show an HTTP 403 response from Elasticsearch when attempting to query the movies index.
root_cause: The LambdaRole policy grants es:ESHttpGet and es:ESHttpPost on the domain-level ARN and on a sub-path ARN restricted to 'other_index/*'. Index-level HTTP operations (like querying movies/_search) require the wildcard sub-path to cover the target index. With the suffix scoped to 'other_index/*', the policy does not authorize requests to the 'movies' index path, causing Elasticsearch to return 403.
